I am 66 years old and have never been to school, but I have farmed this land in Quzhou for over forty years. My family has 10 mu of land, and it is just my wife and me working it now — our son works in a factory in Handan and only comes back to help at harvest.

The wheat is already in the ground. I sowed it last October 1st, right after National Day, like I always do. I plant improved wheat seed, about 30 jin per mu. I will rotary-till the cotton land soon, but for the wheat I already did that last autumn. The wheat needs three irrigations: the winter irrigation to keep it from freezing, one at green-up when the weather warms, and one when the grain is filling. I top-dress with urea twice. I spray three times for weeds and rust. I know this wheat well — if the weather treats us fairly, I should get about 950 jin per mu, and I will harvest it in early June.

As soon as the wheat comes off, I plant summer maize on that same 8 mu. I use hybrid seed, usually Nongda or something the seed dealer recommends. I do not till much for the maize — I plant straight into the wheat stubble to save time and diesel. Maize does not need as much water as wheat; I irrigate twice, at the big trumpet stage and when the grain is filling. I spray three times for borers and weeds. I expect about 1,050 jin per mu, and I aim to harvest before the October holiday.

I keep 2 mu for cotton. Cotton is hard work — my back is not what it used to be, and the bollworm sprays are endless — but it brings cash money that wheat and maize cannot match. I plant improved Guoxinmian seed in late April, rotary-till before sowing, irrigate twice, and spray 12 times through the season. I expect about 500 jin of seed cotton per mu. We pick it by hand, mostly ourselves, selling it to the dealer who drives into the village.

I do not try new crops at my age. I stick to what this soil knows and what my body can still manage.
